key_insight: VideoGPA distills geometry priors from a geometry foundation model into video diffusion training via a self-supervised preference-alignment objective, enabling substantially improved 3D structural consistency across generated video frames.
problem_solved: Video diffusion models produce high-quality frames but often fail to maintain 3D coherence across time (object deformation, spatial drift) because standard denoising objectives don’t explicitly enforce geometric consistency.
method: Leverage a pre-trained geometry foundation model (e.g., depth/pose/3D-aware estimator) to produce geometric cues as supervision.
Distill those geometry priors into the video diffusion model with a self-supervised preference-alignment objective that biases generation toward geometrically consistent solutions.
Design the pipeline to be data-efficient by applying alignment on latent/denoised representations and across temporal frames to enforce 3D-consistent motion and shape.
impact: Practitioners get more temporally and spatially stable video generation with fewer artifacts, which improves downstream use in AR/VR, visual effects, and any application needing multi-frame 3D coherence—without large labeled video datasets.

paper_title: VideoGPA: Distilling Geometry Priors for 3D-Consistent Video Generation
paper_authors: Hongyang Du, Junjie Ye, Xiaoyan Cong, Runhao Li, Jingcheng Ni
